# Results — Study 656 (Dragon Portfolio)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
Chris Cole's (Artemis Capital) **Dragon Portfolio**: a 5-sleeve mix (equities + long
bonds + gold + commodity trend + LONG volatility, published weights **24/18/19/18/21%**)
that survives both inflationary and deflationary regimes where a plain 60/40 book dies.
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current
month is dropped). Fingerprint `3dd12240ccde` (SPY/TLT/GLD/DBC/VXX/SHY price panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily auto-adjusted (total-return) closes, SPY/TLT/GLD/DBC/VXX/SHY, 6,162 rows 2002-01-02 → 2026-06-30. DBMF (2019-05-07→) used only for the side-check. |
| Sleeve inceptions | SPY 1993-01-29 · TLT 2002-07-30 · GLD 2004-11-18 · DBC 2006-02-03 · SHY 2002-07-30 |
| **Named data quirk** | VXX the *product* dates to 2009-01-30, but Barclays halted and relaunched it as "Series B" in Jan-2018 — **yfinance's own VXX tape starts 2018-01-25**, nearly a decade short of the product's history. This is the binding constraint on the full 5-sleeve backtest, not the nominal 2009 launch date. |
| Commodity-trend sleeve | 12-month trailing DBC total return, evaluated at the **prior month's close**, decides the position (long DBC or parked in SHY) for the entire following month — the study's single documented execution lag, calendar-known, zero look-ahead. Warm-up needs 12 months of DBC history, so the sleeve goes live 2007-02. |
| Windows | **Core** (Dragon-lite, no vol sleeve): 2007-02-01 → 2026-06-30, n=4,883 trading days (sees 2008 AND 2020/2022). **Full** (Dragon-full, w/ VXX): 2018-03-01 → 2026-06-30, n=2,094 trading days (misses 2008 entirely; sees 2020/2022). |
| Rebalance / costs | Monthly, reset to target weights on the first trading day of each month; one-way turnover × 5 bps × NAV per rebalance leg (10 bps sensitivity shown below); long-only throughout, **no shorts, no borrow**. |
| Sharpe convention | Excess-of-cash: SHY (T-bill ETF total return) subtracted from every arm before annualising — an apples-to-apples race, not raw-vs-excess. |
| Survivorship | No cross-sectional panel/basket here — every sleeve is a single, currently-listed ETF, so there is no basket survivorship bias to name. **Named instead:** VXX is itself a *relaunched* product (the original Series A was effectively superseded in 2018); our whole "full Dragon" backtest necessarily rides the vehicle era that survived to be listed on Yahoo today. |

## Weights (Cole's published allocation, and the ex-vol renormalisation)

| Sleeve | Proxy | Dragon-full | Dragon-lite (renormalised ex-vol) |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| Equities | SPY | 24% | 30.4% |
| Fixed income | TLT | 18% | 22.8% |
| Gold | GLD | 19% | 24.1% |
| Commodity trend | 12-mo trend overlay on DBC | 18% | 22.8% |
| Long volatility | VXX (named as a crude, decaying proxy) | 21% | — |

Benchmarks: **60/40** (60% SPY / 40% TLT) and **All-Weather-lite** — an *equal-weight*
25/25/25/25 SPY/TLT/GLD/DBC, buy-and-hold, monthly rebalanced. This is **not** Study
[68-all-weather](../../68-all-weather/)'s inverse-vol risk-parity engine — it is a
simpler, static cousin used here only as a same-window comparison point; see the dedup
note in [references.md](references.md).

## The headline — core window (Dragon-lite, no vol sleeve; 2007-02-01 → 2026-06-30)

| Portfolio | CAGR | Vol | Sharpe (ex-cash) | Max DD | Worst 12m |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Dragon-lite (4 sleeve)** | 7.82% | 9.22% | **0.668** | **−26.4%** | **−21.0%** |
| 60/40 SPY/TLT | 8.30% | 11.21% | 0.601 | −31.4% | −26.2% |
| All-Weather-lite | 7.12% | 10.13% | 0.551 | −27.9% | −24.8% |
| 100% SPY | 10.90% | 19.67% | 0.519 | −55.2% | −47.4% |

Ex-vol, the Dragon recipe does genuinely diversify: best Sharpe on the panel, smallest
drawdown and smallest worst-12-month of the four, for a CAGR forfeit of only **0.48
pp/yr** vs 60/40 (far smaller than, e.g., the Permanent Portfolio's ~3.5 pp/yr forfeit
in [Study 144](../../144-permanent-portfolio/)). **But it is not statistically
certified** — see Inference below.

## The headline — full window (Dragon-full w/ VXX; 2018-03-01 → 2026-06-30)

| Portfolio | CAGR | Vol | Sharpe (ex-cash) | Max DD | Worst 12m |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Dragon-full (5 sleeve)** | **−1.28%** | 15.03% | **−0.148** | −45.0% | −24.7% |
| 60/40 SPY/TLT | 8.66% | 12.15% | 0.596 | −27.7% | −25.8% |
| All-Weather-lite | 9.64% | 10.14% | 0.790 | −18.6% | −13.8% |
| 100% SPY | 14.72% | 19.18% | 0.703 | −33.7% | −19.7% |

The moment the real long-vol sleeve is added at its published 21% weight, the whole
portfolio **loses money outright** over the only window we can test it on (CAGR
**−1.28%/yr**) and its Sharpe goes negative — while every benchmark, including the much
simpler All-Weather-lite, comes out solidly positive over the *same* window.

## Crisis windows — the two regimes the claim is built for

**2020 COVID crash, cumulative return 2020-01-01 → 2020-04-30:**

| Dragon-lite | 60/40 | All-Weather-lite | SPY | Dragon-full |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| +3.71% | +3.67% | −2.93% | −9.22% | **+33.35%** |

**2022 full calendar year** (the rare year stocks *and* bonds both fell):

| Dragon-lite | 60/40 | All-Weather-lite | SPY | Dragon-full |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| −9.32% | **−23.32%** | −8.73% | −18.18% | −10.90% |

Both single episodes favor Dragon over 60/40 — dramatically so in 2020 (the VXX sleeve
alone explains almost all of the +30 pp gap) and moderately in 2022 (where Dragon-lite
and All-Weather-lite do just as well *without* any long-vol sleeve — the 2022 cushioning
comes from gold + trend, not specifically from VXX). Two episodes is a demonstration,
not a certified sample — no *t*-stat is claimed on n=2.

## VXX standalone — the "unproxiable cheaply" diagnostic

| Metric | Value |
|---|--:|
| CAGR | **−40.7%/yr** |
| Annualised vol | 73.7% |
| Max drawdown | −99.5% |
| Cumulative buy-and-hold return, 2018-01-26 → 2026-06-30 | **−98.8%** |
| Return during the COVID spike (2020-02-19 → 2020-03-23) | **+271.6%** — this is the payoff it exists for |

VXX is a structurally decaying front-month VIX-futures note: it bled **99% of its
value** over 8.4 years while paying off **+272%** in six trading weeks during the one
episode it was built for. That single spike is nowhere near enough to offset eight
years of contango bleed at 21% portfolio weight — which is exactly why Dragon-full's
aggregate Sharpe over the same window is negative. This is the brutally-honest core
finding: **the long-vol sleeve is not cheaply proxiable** with a buy-and-hold ETN;
Cole's own paper assumes an actively-managed options/variance book, which this study
cannot build from public tape.

## Inference — is the Dragon's edge over 60/40 real, or noise?

| Test | Value |
|---|--:|
| Dragon-lite − 60/40 (core, monthly), mean gap | −0.049%/mo |
| Dragon-lite − 60/40, Newey-West *t* | **−0.37** (n=233 months) |
| Dragon-full − 60/40 (full, monthly), mean gap | −0.801%/mo |
| Dragon-full − 60/40, Newey-West *t* | **−1.65** (n=100 months) |
| Bootstrap Sharpe diff, Dragon-lite vs 60/40 (core) | **+0.067**, 95% CI [−0.257, +0.373], Dragon wins 67% of resamples |
| Bootstrap Sharpe diff, Dragon-full vs 60/40 (full) | **−0.745**, 95% CI [−1.987, +0.357], Dragon wins 9% of resamples |
| Bootstrap Sharpe diff, Dragon-full vs All-Weather-lite (full) | **−0.938**, 95% CI [−1.975, +0.086], Dragon wins 3% of resamples |

None of the three comparisons clears **|t| ≥ 2** (or excludes zero at 95%) in either
direction. The core (ex-vol) Dragon's better point-estimate Sharpe is real-looking on
the chart but **not statistically certified** with 19 years of monthly data; the full
Dragon's *negative* Sharpe gap vs both benchmarks over its 8-year window leans
convincingly negative (Dragon wins only 3-9% of bootstrap resamples) without formally
clearing significance either — the honest read is "probably worse, not certainly."

## Cost sensitivity (Dragon-full, monthly rebalance)

| One-way cost | CAGR | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 bps | −1.24% | −0.146 |
| 5 bps | −1.28% | −0.148 |
| 10 bps | −1.31% | −0.151 |

Transaction costs are a rounding error here (≈3 bps/yr of CAGR from 0→10 bps) — the
whole story is the VXX carry cost, not turnover.

## DBMF side-check — is the DIY trend overlay even a fair proxy?

Real managed-futures ETF (DBMF, live since 2019-05-07) vs our single-index DBC trend
overlay, over their overlapping window (2019-05-09 → 2026-06-30, n=1,795 days):

| | CAGR | Vol |
|---|--:|--:|
| Our TREND proxy (DBC + 12-mo overlay) | +9.4% | 15.3% |
| Real DBMF (multi-market managed futures) | +9.2% | 12.4% |
| Daily return correlation | **+0.28** | |

Similar headline returns by coincidence, but a **+0.28 correlation** is weak — a single
long/flat overlay on one commodity index is a materially cruder proxy for Cole's
"diversified trend across dozens of futures curves" than the DBC ticker alone suggests.
Named honestly: the commodity-trend sleeve, like the long-vol sleeve, is a simplification
the real Dragon Portfolio does not make.

## Synthetic crisis-hedge control — the machinery is (mostly) unbiased

Deterministic monthly 5-asset world; the test isolates the mechanism directly — does
the Dragon-weighted TREND+VOL sub-sleeve (0.18×TREND + 0.21×VOL) pay off **more in
crisis months than normal months**? (Not "Dragon vs 60/40" — a lower equity weight
alone would win any stock crash with zero genuine crisis alpha, which would make a
naive null fire on a pure beta artefact rather than testing the hedge channel.)

| World | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (hedge_strength = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.22** (sd 1.20), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted hedge_strength = 1.0 (seed 656) | **+30.93** |

1/20 ≈ the ~5% nominal false-positive rate of a two-sided |t|≥2 test at this sample
size — not a systematic bias. The detector is silent on the null and lights up hard on
a planted crisis-alpha effect. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in
support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** Ex-vol, the Dragon recipe shows a real-looking risk-adjusted
  edge over 60/40 (Sharpe 0.668 vs 0.601, smaller drawdown, smaller worst-12-month)
  that is **not statistically certified** (HAC *t* = −0.37, bootstrap CI crosses
  zero). Add the real long-vol sleeve at its published weight and the aggregate
  Sharpe over the only testable window (2018-2026) turns **negative** (−0.148 vs
  60/40's 0.596), even though that same sleeve delivered a genuine +33 pp crisis
  payoff in 2020 and helped cushion 2022. Real crisis-window diversification, an
  uncertified aggregate edge, and a costly sleeve that hasn't yet repaid its premium
  on the tape we can see — genuinely split by regime and by leg.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The ex-vol core is close to investable (cheap, liquid
  ETFs, trivial cost drag). But the *published* 5-sleeve allocation, built on the only
  cheaply-tradable long-vol proxy available (VXX), lost money outright over 8+ years —
  the "insurance premium" has not yet been repaid by the 2020 spike it survived. A real
  implementation would need an actively-managed options/variance book this study
  cannot cheaply replicate from public tape.
- **"A cheap ETF Dragon just works?" — BUSTED.** The diversification kernel (equity +
  bonds + gold + trend) genuinely helps in both a deflationary shock (2020) and an
  inflationary both-down year (2022) — that part of the myth holds up. But "cheap"
  fails outright: the only publicly tradable long-volatility instrument bled 99% of its
  value over the sample, turning the full prescribed portfolio Sharpe-negative even
  though it contains two crisis wins. You cannot buy this portfolio off the shelf and
  expect it to work the way the paper says — not yet, not on this tape.
